resources.string: ReelGuard watches for the Instagram share sheet and closes it right away, so you cannot send reels. It only looks at screen text inside Instagram, never reads your messages, and does not use the internet.
ReelGuard is watching Instagram and closes the share sheet the moment it opens.
Turn ReelGuard on in Accessibility so it can close the share sheet before a reel leaves your phone.
Android 13 and newer: if Android won’t let you turn it on, open App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings.
Why can’t I turn it on?
One count is one share stopped before it left your phone.
Today’s and all-time counts go back to zero. Your streak, start date, and blocking stay on.
Show “Share blocked” each time a sheet is closed.
Only windows from Instagram, Instagram Lite, and Instagram Basel are inspected.
When the sheet appears, ReelGuard presses Back before you can send.
Each blocked share is counted locally. Instagram is never modified.
No internet permission, no analytics, no accounts. Counters and settings stay on this phone.
ReelGuard needs Android’s Accessibility permission to see Instagram’s share sheet and close it.
Find and turn on “ReelGuard share blocker”.
Come back here to confirm the status says Active.
Android 13 and newer blocks Accessibility for apps installed outside a store. If the toggle is unavailable, open App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then try again.
Instagram changes its screens sometimes. If blocking stops working after an Instagram update, ReelGuard may need an update too.
